  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not put big data in a static singleton to avoid parceling (dies with the process, causing a different bug); and I would not compress bytes into the Bundle to squeeze under the limit.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Does largeHeap help? → No, the limit is Binder buffer, not heap.
  • Why does it only crash when backgrounding? → State is saved and sent to the system server when the Activity stops (API 24+ throws).
  • Can you use a bound service to share the list? → It still passes via Binder unless via shared memory or file.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A news app saved a full article object per tab; with 12 tabs open it crashed on backgrounding for power users only, which analytics showed as 0.3% of users but 40% of revenue.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Try/catch, or blames fragments.
  • Hire: Identifies the 1 MB Binder limit with the math, passes IDs.
  • Strong hire: Adds SavedStateHandle/repository design, debug-size assertion, and explains why the stop-time save is where it surfaces.

questions.contextHtml:
A fintech app (3M MAU) receives a pentest report: "High: Intent redirection in AuthBridgeActivity". Play Console also shows a security warning on the latest release. The activity is used by the partner SDK to hand over from a bank's app after login:

class AuthBridgeActivity : AppCompatActivity() {          // exported=true, filter: com.fin.action.AUTH_DONE
    override fun onCreate(s: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(s)
        val token = intent.getStringExtra("token")
        session.store(token)
        val next = intent.getParcelableExtra<Intent>("redirect")   // deprecated getter
        if (next != null) startActivity(next)
        finish()
    }
}

The partner app (4 bank apps, 600k installs combined) depends on redirect to resume a flow. A 2-week release freeze starts in 3 days. The pentester's PoC opened the internal, non-exported ExportStatementsActivity.
questions.promptHtml: How do you respond: triage, fix without breaking partners, and prevention?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Set exported=false" (breaks all partner flows) or "check that redirect is not null" (does nothing).

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is the token also attacker-settable (session fixation)? Which partner screens use redirect? Can partners change code within 3 days? Do we have telemetry on redirect targets? Is the finding exploitable remotely or needs a malicious installed app?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Stop launching the supplied Intent now: ship a hotfix before the freeze that ignores redirect unless it resolves to an allowlisted component. Add a remote config switch for the allowlist.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) attacker targets any non-exported activity; (b) URI grant flags smuggled via the nested Intent; (c) setResult variants elsewhere; (d) token injection.
  4. How I'd verify each: Write a PoC attacker APK or adb shell am start -n com.fin/.AuthBridgeActivity --ei ...; grep for getParcelableExtra<Intent>, startActivity( with external inputs; run lint UnsafeIntentLaunch; check Crashlytics logs for what redirect values exist in production.
  5. Root cause: Confused deputy. The exported activity launches an attacker-chosen Intent with my UID, so exported=false components, permissions, and URI grants are reachable. Flags such as FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION could also expose my FileProvider.
  6. Fix:
    • Hotfix: replace redirect with a route code and map to known screens; strip all flags.
val route = intent.getStringExtra("route")
val dest = when (route) {
    "dashboard" -> DashboardActivity::class.java
    "transfer"  -> TransferActivity::class.java
    else        -> HomeActivity::class.java
}
startActivity(Intent(this, dest))
  • Keep accepting redirect for one release but only if redirect.component?.packageName == packageName and class is in an allowlist; log violations.
  • Longer term: signature permission or verify caller callingActivity?.packageName against partner allowlist with certificate hashes (PackageManager.getPackageInfo signing info).
  1. Prevention: Lint + security review checklist (any exported component that calls startActivity/sendBroadcast with data derived from input), automated manifest audit listing exported components, annual external pentest.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not rely on callingPackage alone (spoofable when not via startActivityForResult), and would not break partner flows unannounced; I coordinate deprecation dates.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Partner cannot update for 3 months. → Keep the legacy path behind the allowlist for their known targets only.
  • Could an attacker launch the activity from a web page? → Only if BROWSABLE filter exists; here there is none, so a malicious installed app is required.
  • What about Intent.parseUri in WebView bridges? → Same class of bug; use Intent.URI_INTENT_SCHEME and strip component/selector.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "trampoline" activity added for a marketing SDK stayed exported for two years. An internal red team used it to reach a hidden debug screen on production builds.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Null checks or blanket exported=false.
  • Hire: Allowlist mapping, route codes, mitigation and PoC.
  • Strong hire: Handles partner compatibility, URI-grant flag stripping, caller verification limits, and prevention automation.

questions.contextHtml:
A super-app (6M DAU) raises targetSdk 29 to 33 in one jump. Within two days of staged rollout at 50%, support tickets spike: "Pay with UPI app button missing", "cannot open Maps", "Invite via WhatsApp does nothing". Crash rate is flat at 0.3%, but UPI payment conversion on Android 11+ falls from 61% to 38%. The UPI code:

val upi = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse("upi://pay?pa=$vpa&am=$amt"))
val apps = pm.queryIntentActivities(upi, 0)       // shows installed UPI apps as buttons
if (apps.isEmpty()) showCardOnly()

and getPackageInfo("com.whatsapp", 0) wrapped in try/catch returning false. Android 10 and below show no regression (35% of base).
questions.promptHtml: Diagnose, mitigate, and describe a fix that is Play-policy compliant.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES" immediately. It may be rejected, over-exposes, and ignores the intent-based approach.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is the drop only on API 30+? Is it only for targetSdk 33 builds? Is startActivity still working when called blindly? Which features rely on query APIs?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Pause the rollout at 50%; a feature flag to show a generic "Pay with UPI" button using createChooser rather than a per-app list while a fix is built.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) package visibility filtering (matches API split); (b) a payments SDK needs its own <queries>; (c) a server config changed (red herring: only the build changed); (d) Play Protect or OEM issue.
  4. How I'd verify each: Compare conversion by OS version; run the same code on API 29 and API 30 emulators with targetSdk 33 and log queryIntentActivities().size; check the merged manifest for <queries>; adb shell dumpsys package to confirm UPI apps are installed.
  5. Root cause: Targeting 30+ filters queryIntentActivities and getPackageInfo to visible packages; no <queries> means empty results, so UI hides options.
  6. Fix:
<queries>
  <intent><action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/><data android:scheme="upi" android:host="pay"/></intent>
  <intent><action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/><data android:scheme="geo"/></intent>
  <package android:name="com.whatsapp"/>
</queries>

Prefer intent queries over package lists. For launching only, skip queries entirely and catch ActivityNotFoundException. 7. Prevention: Keep targetSdk-change checklist reading the behaviour-change pages; test matrix including API 30+; instrumented tests asserting queryIntentActivities non-empty on a device image with a stub UPI app; analytics funnel alerts by OS version. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not use QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES (Play requires a declared core-purpose justification; a payment-method picker is typically served by intent queries). I'd not enumerate competitor packages that the user did not choose to expose.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Why did the crash rate stay flat? → Failures were silent: empty lists and caught exceptions.
  • Is startActivity blocked by missing visibility? → No; that is why the blind launch still works, which is a valid fallback.
  • A library's manifest adds many <queries>; problem? → Merged queries reveal the app list to Play reviewers; review the merged manifest.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A map-based app lost directions on Android 11 because resolveActivity(geo:) returned null; engineers saw nothing in logs since the feature simply hid.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Does not connect the OS split to the cause.
  • Hire: Identifies package visibility, adds intent <queries>.
  • Strong hire: Compares launch vs query behavior, Play policy for QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, and adds observability so silent failures surface.

questions.contextHtml: Your notes app (2M MAU) wants to be a share target for text, images, and PDFs from any app, and to handle "Open with" for .md files. Product also wants a custom notes://new?title= scheme for automation apps. Security wants a minimal attack surface after last quarter's redirection finding. Constraints: images up to 25 MB, p95 share-to-editor under 400 ms on mid-range devices, Android 8 (API 26) to 15.
questions.promptHtml: Design the intent-facing layer: components, filters, validation, and what you refuse to support.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: One exported MainActivity with every filter, reading EXTRA_STREAM on the main thread, and parsing any extras into navigation.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Do we need multiple shares at once (SEND_MULTIPLE)? Who are the automation apps (known partners or arbitrary)? Do shared files need to persist after the source app dies? Is Direct Share needed?
  2. Immediate mitigation: N/A (design). Start with the principle: every exported entry is a public API.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked (design options): (a) single exported trampoline ShareReceiverActivity that only ingests then launches an internal explicit Intent; (b) multiple exported activities per filter; (c) custom scheme with auto-run commands vs read-only prefill.
  4. How I'd verify each: Fuzz with adb shell am start sending huge, malformed, wrong-MIME extras; StrictMode disk/network violations; Perfetto trace for share-to-editor time; Monkey on the receiver.
  5. Root cause / rationale: Single narrow ingress point gives one place for validation. Heavy work must not be in the exported component's lifecycle.
  6. Design:
    • ShareReceiverActivity (exported, taskAffinity separate, excludeFromRecents false): filters for ACTION_SEND and SEND_MULTIPLE with specific MIME types (not */*).
    • It validates type, copies streams to app cache with a size cap (25 MB) on Dispatchers.IO, using contentResolver.openInputStream, then starts the internal non-exported EditorActivity explicitly with IDs of the cached items.
    • Intent-based reads use IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(..., Uri::class.java) and ignore nested Intents completely.
    • notes://new?title= only prefills a draft (no destructive actions, no auto-send), with title capped at 200 chars.
    • Publish sharing shortcuts for Direct Share (API 29+ via ShortcutManagerCompat).
  7. Prevention: CI manifest audit that lists exported components and fails on additions; fuzz tests; Lint UnsafeIntentLaunch.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: No */* filter (spam in the chooser, bigger attack surface); no destructive commands in the custom scheme; no persistable URI permissions unless the user explicitly opts in; accept ~50 ms extra from the copy step to avoid holding a transient grant that expires.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Source app revokes access mid-read? → Catch SecurityException/FileNotFoundException, show error, no crash.
  • Why copy rather than keep the URI? → The grant lasts only while the receiving task lives; copying makes it durable.
  • 10x bigger files? → Stream with progress, use WorkManager for long copies.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: An app read a 40 MB shared PDF into a ByteArray in onCreate, causing ANRs for 1 in 200 shares from file managers.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Exported main activity, */*, main-thread IO.
  • Hire: Single ingress, validates and copies off main thread, explicit hand-off.
  • Strong hire: Grant lifetime, scheme restrictions, fuzzing and CI manifest audit, explicit refusals.

questions.contextHtml: Post-incident review for a retail app (4M MAU). Last Tuesday an email campaign sent 2.4M links https://shop.example/p/123. Expected: 35% open in the app. Measured: 4% on Android 12+, 31% on Android 10-11, and Chrome on iOS fine. No release shipped that week. Two days before, infra moved shop.example behind a CDN that now redirects /.well-known/assetlinks.json with a 302 to a regional path. Support also sees "Open with" chooser dialogs on old devices. The product manager asks whether to "just add a custom scheme."
questions.promptHtml: Give your root-cause analysis and what you change in process and code.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Users disabled links" or "switch to a custom scheme". It addresses symptoms, loses verified security, and ignores the redirect.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: When did the app last verify (install/update)? Does pm get-app-links show verified on affected devices? Did the CDN change affect the file's content type and redirect behaviour? Is the Play signing key in the file?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Fix the CDN to serve the file directly (200, application/json, no redirect); for devices needing re-verification, pm verify-app-links --re-verify is dev-only, so for users, a new app update or Android's periodic re-verification is needed; meanwhile make the web landing page show an "Open in app" button using the app link/intent fallback.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) assetlinks redirect, since verification does not follow redirects; (b) wrong fingerprint; (c) autoVerify filter polluted by a custom host failing; (d) user overrides (red herring at this scale).
  4. How I'd verify each: curl -I https://shop.example/.well-known/assetlinks.json to see 302; Google's Digital Asset Links API check; adb shell pm get-app-links com.example.shop shows verified/none; compare by OS (Android 12 changed unverified behavior: link goes to the browser instead of a chooser).
  5. Root cause: The CDN's 302 made verification fail on new installs and updates after the change. On Android 6-11, unverified links still show app in a chooser (so 31% opened it), while on Android 12+ unverified links go straight to the browser, producing 4%.
  6. Fix: Serve the file directly at the path with correct content type; add a synthetic monitor fetching the file hourly with the exact checks (status 200, JSON valid, includes package and Play signing SHA-256); keep intent filter autoVerify with only the verified hosts; and add ACTION_APP_OPEN_BY_DEFAULT_SETTINGS guidance for users.
  7. Prevention: Treat /.well-known as production-critical in CDN config review; synthetic monitor + alert; release checklist with pm get-app-links on API 31+ test devices; campaign pre-flight test on Android 12+ and 14.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I'd not add a custom scheme as the primary path (any app can claim it; no verification); I'd keep it only as a fallback behind a landing page.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Does fixing the file instantly fix users? → No; devices re-verify on install/update or periodically, so there is lag; communicate that expectation.
  • Why would Android 10 users look fine? → Disambiguation dialog lets them choose the app.
  • Could subdomains be a problem? → Each host needs its own assetlinks file (wildcards in the filter need the base domain file).

sections.html: A migration to a new CDN silently added an x-robots redirect rule; links broke for weeks because nobody owned /.well-known monitoring.
